name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+19 partisan lean makes this one of the safest Democratic House seats
Quigley holds a roughly $1.2M-to-$0 cash-on-hand advantage over Hanson
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 97%

model.rationale: A nineteen-point Democratic district, an entrenched incumbent with a seven-figure war chest, and a challenger showing no fundraising or outside support leave almost no path for a Republican upset, and markets agree at roughly 97 percent Democratic odds.
model.watch: A late-breaking scandal or a suddenly funded challenger campaign could narrow the margin, though nothing currently signals a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois' fifth district carries a partisan lean of nineteen points toward Democrats, making it one of the safest Democratic seats on the House map. Incumbent Mike Quigley returns with about $1.2 million in cash after raising roughly $726,000, while Republican Tommy Hanson shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand. No outside groups are spending for or against either candidate.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price Democratic chances near 97 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a one-sided financial picture points to a comfortable Quigley win. The main uncertainty is turnout in a low-profile contest rather than any genuine competitive threat.
